name: Cortistatin-14
lead: Cortistatin-14 is a naturally occurring neuropeptide related to somatostatin. It was named for its predominantly cortical expression and its ability to depress cortical activity, and it shares 11 of its 14 amino acids with somatostatin-14 even though the two peptides are encoded by separate genes [2][7].

Unlike somatostatin, cortistatin has been reported to bind growth hormone secretagogue (GHS) receptors in human pituitary tissue, and it binds all five cloned somatostatin receptors [2][6]. More recently, structural work identified it as an endogenous agonist of the itch-related receptor MRGPRX2 [1]. It is a research peptide and has no approved medical use.

No published human study has tested cortistatin-14 for any appearance-related purpose. The literature consists of basic neuroscience, receptor pharmacology and a small number of human endocrine studies.

paras: Cortistatin was cloned from human, mouse and rat sources and is known to bind all five cloned somatostatin receptors, sharing many pharmacological properties with somatostatin while also having distinct physiological functions [2][7].

A study of human pituitary membranes reported that cortistatin, but not somatostatin, bound to GHS receptors, the same receptor family targeted by ghrelin [6]. Ghrelin binding sites have also been characterised in human hypothalamus and pituitary tissue [4].

Cryo-electron microscopy structures of MRGPRX2, a mast-cell and itch receptor, bound to cortistatin-14 were published in 2021, identifying the peptide as an endogenous ligand of that receptor [1][5][8].

No studies of cortistatin-14 for appearance, muscle, recovery or growth outcomes were found. A human endocrine study examined the peptide's activities and its interaction with GHRH and ghrelin [9]. Other work is laboratory-based, including receptor expression in human macrophages for somatostatin receptor subtypes [3] and somatostatin knockout mouse studies [10].
No looksmaxxing community discussion of cortistatin-14 was located.

timeline.event: Cloning and chromosomal mapping of mouse and human preprocortistatin reported [7].

card.summary: A somatostatin-related brain peptide that also binds ghrelin-type receptors; basic science only, nothing on looks.
card.note: No human data for any appearance use.

quick.overview:
Cortistatin-14 is a short neuropeptide closely related to somatostatin, first noted for its activity in the cortex. It has been studied in receptor pharmacology and neuroscience.

No published trial has tested it for appearance, muscle or recovery, and it is not an approved drug.
quick.mechanism: It binds all five somatostatin receptors, has been reported to bind GHS (ghrelin-type) receptors in human pituitary, and activates the itch receptor MRGPRX2.
quick.risks: Human safety data are essentially limited to small endocrine studies. It has no approved product or regulatory status as a medicine.
